votes.motion: Approve the amended formal meeting minutes of June 8, 2021
votes.description: The Council approved corrections to the formal meeting minutes from June 8, 2021.

votes.motion: Adopt Joint Ceremonial Resolution 18 of 2022: recognizing July 19, 2022, as 'One Kind Act A Day' day in Salt Lake City
votes.description: The Council adopted a joint ceremonial resolution with the Mayor recognizing 'One Kind Act A Day' day (later corrected to the week of September 12, 2022) in Salt Lake City, honoring the Semnani Family Foundation's initiative.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and refer Items B-1 through B-2 to a future Consent Agenda for action
votes.description: The Council closed the public hearing on two Police Department grant applications (COPS Grant and State of Utah Asset Forfeiture Grant) and referred them to a future Consent Agenda for action.

votes.motion: Suspend the rules and adopt Ordinance 42 of 2022 Updating Salt Lake City Corporation's practices regarding donations to the City, with specified changes
votes.description: The Council suspended the rules to adopt an ordinance establishing policy and guidelines for the City's acceptance of donations, including a review process and reporting requirements to the City Council.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 43 of 2022 Convention on the Elimination of all Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW) and Gender Equity, enacting chapter 10.08 of the Salt Lake City Code pertaining to gender equality
votes.description: The Council adopted an ordinance establishing gender equity requirements including intersectional gender analysis every five years, oversight by the Chief Equity Officer, and an equal pay for equal work compensation policy.

votes.motion: Adopt Resolution 19 of 2022 Transit Master Plan Implementation Interlocal Agreement with the Utah Transit Authority (UTA)
votes.description: The Council adopted a resolution authorizing the Mayor to enter into two amendments to an interlocal agreement with UTA, providing accounting adjustments for COVID-19 related service reductions and adding Frequent Transit Network service agreements for several routes.

The Council approved the Consent Agenda, which included setting public hearing dates for several zoning and rezone items and approving board appointments for Matthew Morriss to the Bicycle Advisory Committee and Brad Christensen to the CDCIP Advisory Board.
